hero.eyebrow: Workplace skills · No software to install
hero.title: Business Communication: write and speak so people act
hero.subtitle: Write emails, memos and updates in a document editor, and cost your meetings in a working spreadsheet. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can write clear emails and memos, run efficient meetings and give feedback with confidence.

assessment: Finish the required labs in each module: they are checked automatically and explained when something is missing.
Pass each module quiz (70% or more). You can retry as often as you like.
Complete the project update and the final assessment.

faq.a: No. It focuses on clarity, structure and tone in workplace situations; the labs check for structure and specific content rather than grammar.

faq.q: Does it suit non-native English speakers?
faq.a: Yes. The principles of short sentences, plain words and clear structure help everyone, and one module covers writing for international readers.
You earn a completion badge on this platform. It is not an externally accredited qualification.

activities.title: Write a clear request email
activities.objective: Write an email whose purpose is obvious in the first lines and whose next step is clear.
activities.scenario: You need your manager to approve leave from 10 to 14 March. Write the email.
steps: Start with a Subject: line that states the request.
Greet the reader (Dear or Hello).
In the first sentence say what you want and the dates.
Add one or two lines of reason or handover plan.
State the decision you need and the date you need it by.
End with Thank you and your name.

checks.label: A subject line
checks.hint: Begin with Subject: and a short, specific line.
checks.explain: The subject tells the reader what the email is about before they open it.

checks.label: A greeting
checks.hint: Start with Dear or Hello and a name.
checks.explain: A greeting sets a respectful tone.

checks.label: The dates appear
checks.explain: A request without exact dates cannot be approved.

checks.label: A clear ask
checks.hint: Say please approve or I would like to request.
checks.explain: State what you need in plain words.

spec.what: a clear request such as approve

checks.label: A reply date
checks.hint: Say by when you need an answer, such as by Friday.
checks.explain: A deadline helps the reader prioritise.

spec.what: a date such as by Friday

checks.label: A polite closing
checks.hint: End with Thank you or Regards.
checks.explain: A courteous ending completes the message.

checks.label: Short: 50 to 150 words
checks.hint: Cut anything that does not help.

activities.title: Rewrite a rambling message
activities.objective: Cut a long, vague email down to a short, specific one.
activities.scenario: The original says: 'Hi, I was just wondering, if it is not too much trouble, whether you might possibly have some time at some point soon to look at the thing we spoke about.' Rewrite it as a clear request.
steps: Name the document or task (the budget file).
Add a specific deadline (Thursday).
Keep it under 40 words and polite.

checks.label: Names the item
checks.explain: Say what you mean, not 'the thing'.

checks.label: Gives a deadline
checks.explain: A date is easier to act on than 'soon'.

checks.label: Avoids hedging phrases
checks.hint: Remove 'possibly', 'wondering' and 'if it is not too much trouble'.

activities.title: Write a one-page memo
activities.objective: Write a memo that leads with the recommendation, then the reasons, then the next steps.
activities.scenario: Your team shares one slow printer. Recommend replacing it, citing the cost of lost time.
steps: Add a heading with the memo title.
Add three Heading 2 sections: Recommendation, Reasons and Next steps.
Give the recommendation in the first section in one or two sentences.
List at least three reasons in a bulleted list.
List the next steps in a numbered list.
Keep it between 100 and 260 words.

checks.label: A title heading
checks.explain: A memo needs a clear subject.

checks.label: Three sections
checks.explain: Clear sections let readers jump to what they need.

checks.label: A numbered list of steps
checks.explain: Numbers show the order of action.

activities.title: What does a meeting cost?
activities.objective: Calculate the real cost of a meeting so you can decide whether it is worth holding.
activities.scenario: A weekly status meeting has six attendees. Work out its yearly cost and what shortening it would save.
steps: In C2 enter the hourly cost: monthly pay divided by 160 hours.
In D2 enter the cost of the meeting for that person: hourly cost times hours in the meeting (B9).
Fill down to row 7.
In D8 total the meeting cost.
In B10 multiply by 48 weeks for the yearly cost.
In B11 calculate the yearly saving if the meeting is cut to 30 minutes.

checks.label: C2 is Asha's hourly cost
checks.explain: Pay per month over 160 working hours.

checks.label: D2 is Asha's meeting cost
checks.explain: Lock B9 so it stays fixed.

checks.label: D7 is filled down
checks.hint: Fill the formulas down to row 7.

checks.label: B11 is the saving from a shorter meeting
checks.explain: Halving the length halves the cost.

activities.title: Draft a meeting agenda
activities.objective: Write an agenda with a purpose, timed items, owners and expected outcomes.
activities.scenario: You are chairing a 30-minute project meeting to decide the launch date.
steps: Add a heading 'Agenda: Launch date decision'.
Write one sentence of purpose.
Add a numbered list of at least four items, each with minutes in brackets and an owner.
End with a line starting Decision needed:.

checks.label: A purpose sentence
checks.explain: People should know why they are meeting.

activities.title: Give feedback with the SBI model
activities.objective: Describe the Situation, the Behaviour and the Impact, then agree a next step.
activities.scenario: A colleague interrupted you three times in a client meeting yesterday. Write what you would say.
steps: Write three short paragraphs starting with Situation:, Behaviour: and Impact:.
Describe only what you saw and heard, not what you assume about their motives.
Finish with a line starting Request: asking for a specific change.

checks.label: An Impact line
checks.explain: Say the effect on you or the work.

checks.label: A Request line
checks.explain: A request turns feedback into change.

checks.label: In the right order
checks.explain: The model follows a natural logic.

checks.label: Avoids blaming words
checks.hint: Avoid always, never and you are.

spec.what: no always, never or you are

activities.title: Write a working-agreement for a remote team
activities.objective: Set clear team rules for channels, response times and time zones.
activities.scenario: Your team of six works from two countries. Write a short communication agreement.
steps: Add a heading 'Team communication agreement'.
Add at least four rules as a bulleted list.
Mention a response time, a time zone or core hours, and which channel is for urgent matters.
Keep it between 70 and 200 words.

checks.label: At least four rules in a list
checks.explain: Short rules are easy to remember.

checks.label: A response time
checks.explain: Without a response time people wait in doubt.

spec.what: a response time such as 24 hours

checks.label: Time zones or core hours
checks.hint: Mention a time zone or core hours.

spec.what: a time zone or core hours

checks.label: How to reach someone urgently
checks.hint: Mention urgent matters and the channel.
checks.explain: Everyone must know the escalation route.

checks.label: Between 70 and 200 words
checks.explain: Agreements that are too long are ignored.

activities.title: Final project: write a communication pack
activities.objective: Write a short pack for one project update: a summary, an email and a list of actions.
activities.scenario: A project is two weeks late because a supplier delayed delivery. Write the update for your manager.
steps: Add a Heading 1 'Project update'.
Under a Heading 2 'Summary' write two or three sentences stating the situation, the cause and the new date.
Under a Heading 2 'Options' list at least two options in a bulleted list.
Under a Heading 2 'Recommendation' write one or two sentences.
Under a Heading 2 'Actions' write a numbered list of at least three actions with owners and dates.
Keep it between 130 and 330 words.

checks.label: Four sections
checks.hint: Use Heading 2 for Summary, Options, Recommendation and Actions.
checks.explain: Structure lets the manager decide quickly.

checks.label: Sections in order
checks.explain: Lead with the situation, end with action.

checks.label: A new date is given
checks.explain: A delay without a new date is unfinished.
